items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I spent a lot of time with her, thinking we were going to do something together.

ctx.x: Katherine Dunham was going to help me for a while (inaudible). Because I'm not a dancer. I could tell her the story and she could do the choreography. I spent a lot of time with her, thinking we were going to do something together. But she had more things on her mind than to want to (inaudible) help me through my [You know, ballet people] ballet, my operatic ballet. (inaudible) would do a dance and sing at the same time, we wouldn't have to worry about classical voices other than the role of the elite white…

I'm just trying to say that I ended up doing something that was just about one half of what I really wanted to do, what I was capable of doing. So you get into a rut, of just doing the simplest things. (inaudible) Maybe this illness that's on me now is 'cause I'm going to get my solfege together, got to really get my ears together and got to be able to say what I want -- what I hear in my head. I haven't got the complete use of my arms, like I should have. It's going to come back,
